how_to_read.relevant_record_ids: store record ids whose chunk holds the answer; retrieval is a hit when any is retrieved. The first is the best one

questions.question: What output voltage range and output current does the LM317 support?
questions.expected_answer: An adjustable output from 1.25 V to 37 V, and more than 1.5 A of output current (1.5 A in the recommended operating conditions).

questions.question: How much input-to-output headroom does the LM317 need to stay in regulation, and what happens with less?
questions.expected_answer: Up to 3 V of headroom (VI - VO). With less, the device can drop out and the output becomes the input voltage minus the dropout voltage.

questions.question: When does the LM317 need an input bypass capacitor, and how large should it be?
questions.expected_answer: When the device is more than six inches from the input filter capacitors. Any type works for stability, and it should be 0.1 uF or greater.
questions.notes: Chunk 29 has both conditions; chunks 1 and 2 give the six inches but not the size.

questions.question: In the slow turn-on 15 V regulator circuit, what voltage does the output start at, and why?
questions.expected_answer: 1.9 V: the capacitor C1 starts uncharged, so VOUT = VC1 + VBE + 1.25 V = 0 V + 0.65 V + 1.25 V. VOUT then rises with the capacitor voltage until the PNP turns off.
questions.notes: The circuit's figure (Figure 8-13) was not captured at ingestion; chunk 26 has no image.

questions.question: In the 50 mA constant-current battery charger, what sets the charge current and what input voltage does it need?
questions.expected_answer: ICHG = 1.25 V / 24 ohm, about 52 mA (the circuit is named 50 mA). VI must be greater than VBAT + 4.25 V (1.25 V reference plus 3 V headroom).
questions.notes: Ingestion trap: chunk 25's stored text reads the resistor as '240' (OCR error). An answer with 240 ohm or about 5 mA shows the error reached the answer.

questions.question: What are the LM317's recommended operating conditions?
questions.expected_answer: Output voltage 1.25 V to 37 V; input-to-output differential 3 V to 40 V; output current 0.01 A to 1.5 A; operating virtual junction temperature 0 C to 125 C.
questions.notes: Section 6.3 sits in the ESD ratings chunk (8), not in the absolute maximum ratings chunk (7).

questions.question: What is the junction-to-ambient thermal resistance of the new-chip LM317 in the SOT-223 and TO-263 packages?
questions.expected_answer: 59.6 C/W for SOT-223 (DCY) and 41.0 C/W for TO-263 (KTT).
questions.notes: Trap: the legacy-chip table (chunk 9) gives 66.8 and 38.0 for the same packages.

questions.question: What minimum load current does the LM317 need to stay in regulation?
questions.expected_answer: 3.5 mA typical and 10 mA maximum, at VIN - VOUT = 40 V over the full operating temperature range.
questions.notes: Section 7.4.3 (chunk 18) points to the table without a value.

questions.question: What ripple rejection does the new-chip LM317 achieve at 120 Hz with a 10 uF adjust-pin capacitor?
questions.expected_answer: 66 dB minimum, 80 dB typical, at VOUT = 10 V, f = 120 Hz, CADJ = 10 uF, over the full operating temperature range. Without CADJ it is 65 dB typical.
questions.notes: Page 1 states 80 dB at 120 Hz for CADJ = 10 uF (new chip) in the features list.

questions.question: In the typical application circuit on the first page, what are the component values?
questions.expected_answer: R1 = 240 ohm (OUTPUT to ADJ), R2 = 5 kohm adjustable (ADJ to GND), C1 = 0.1 uF on the input (needed if more than 6 inches from the filter capacitors), C2 = 1 uF on the output (optional, improves transient response), with VIN >= 28 V.
questions.notes: Values are only in the figure (dbv2/images/lm317_c2_img0.jpg); the page text has them only partly and out of order.

questions.question: What is the pinout of the LM317 in the 4-pin SOT-223 (DCY) package?
questions.expected_answer: Pin 1 ADJUST, pin 2 OUTPUT, pin 3 INPUT, and pin 4 (the tab) OUTPUT.
questions.notes: Ingestion trap: chunk 6's stored table reads ADJUST as pin '1 4 1' (OCR). The figure (lm317_c6_img0.jpg) is clear.

questions.question: How does the new-chip LM317's reference voltage change with temperature?
questions.expected_answer: It peaks at about 1.250 V near 25 C, is about 1.245 V at -55 C, and falls to about 1.232 V at 150 C (Figure 6-19).
questions.notes: Values are read from a graph, so accept about +/- 0.003 V. Same image as Figure 6-20 (quiescent current), 6-21 and 6-22.

questions.question: How does copper area on the PCB affect the TO-263 package's junction-to-ambient thermal resistance?
questions.expected_answer: It drops from about 74 C/W with almost no copper to about 35 C/W at 1 square inch; beyond 1 square inch there is very little improvement. The minimum on a PCB is 32 C/W (1 oz copper).
questions.notes: Figure 8-21 (lm317_c32_img0.jpg) plus the text below it.

questions.question: What is the LM317's built-in soft-start time?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated: the LM317 has no built-in soft-start. The datasheet only shows an external slow turn-on circuit (Figure 8-13) with no time given.
questions.notes: A good answer may mention the external slow turn-on circuit but must not invent a time. Cross-document trap: the TLV1117 fixed version does have an internal soft-start.

questions.question: What is the LM317's RMS output noise from 10 Hz to 100 kHz?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated for that bandwidth. The datasheet gives 0.003 % of VOUT typical for 10 Hz to 10 kHz only.
questions.notes: Fails if it presents the 10 kHz figure as the 100 kHz one, or converts it to uV without saying so.

questions.question: At what junction temperature does the LM317's thermal shutdown trip?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated. The datasheet says the device has internal thermal shutdown and gives a rated maximum junction temperature of 125 C (new chip), but no trip temperature.
questions.notes: Cross-document trap: the TLV1117 datasheet gives 180 C shutdown and 160 C reset (new chip, fixed output); using them for the LM317 is a failure. Quoting 125 C as the trip point is also a failure: that is the rated maximum.

questions.question: What input voltage range, output current and output voltage options does the TLV1117 offer?
questions.expected_answer: Input 2.7 V to 15 V, up to 800 mA of output current, fixed outputs from 1.5 V to 5 V, and an adjustable output from 1.25 V to 13.8 V.

questions.question: Does the TLV1117 need a minimum load current?
questions.expected_answer: The adjustable version needs at least 1.7 mA of load current for stable operation (1.7 mA typical, 5 mA maximum at VIN = 15 V). The fixed version (new chip) has no minimum load requirement.

questions.question: How does the TLV1117's foldback current limit work?
questions.expected_answer: It is a hybrid brick-wall and foldback limit (fixed output, new chip). Above VFOLDBACK = 50% of VOUT(nom), the output current is held at the current limit ICL. Below it, the limit folds back towards the short-circuit current ISC as the output approaches ground. If thermal shutdown triggers, the device cycles between current limit and thermal shutdown.
questions.notes: The figure (tlv1117_c22_img0.jpg) shows the same shape.

questions.question: Does the adjustable TLV1117 need protection diodes?
questions.expected_answer: Not in normal operation: the ADJ pin withstands a +/-25 V transient relative to the output, and the internal output-to-input diode handles microsecond surges of 10 A to 20 A. With a very large output capacitor (1000 uF or more) and the input shorted to ground, add an external diode from output to input.
questions.notes: Ingestion trap: chunk 29 stores '>= 1000 uF' as '21000uUF' (OCR).

questions.question: What is the TLV1117's dropout voltage at 800 mA?
questions.expected_answer: New chip, fixed output: 0.8 V typical, 1.2 V maximum. Otherwise (legacy and adjustable): 1.2 V typical, 1.3 V maximum (C version) or 1.4 V maximum (I version).
questions.notes: Two rows for the same parameter; an answer must say which chip each value belongs to.

questions.question: At what temperature does the TLV1117's thermal shutdown trip and reset?
questions.expected_answer: Shutdown at 180 C (temperature increasing) and reset at 160 C (temperature falling), for the new chip with fixed output.
questions.notes: The two values are split across chunks 11 and 12.

questions.question: What is the TLV1117's quiescent current?
questions.expected_answer: New chip, fixed output: 65 uA typical, 110 uA maximum (IOUT = 0 mA, VIN = 15 V); page 1 rounds the typical to 60 uA. Adjustable output: 5 mA typical, 10 mA maximum (C) or 15 mA maximum (I).
questions.notes: Page 1 (60 uA) and the table (65 uA) differ; either is acceptable if attributed.

questions.question: What input voltage does the TLV1117-33 (3.3 V fixed) need, and what output current is it rated for?
questions.expected_answer: 4.7 V to 15 V input, and up to 0.8 A output current (Recommended Operating Conditions).

questions.question: What are the pin assignments of the TLV1117 in its 3-pin and SOT-223 packages?
questions.expected_answer: Pin 1 ADJ/GND (adjust for the adjustable version, ground for fixed), pin 2 OUTPUT, pin 3 INPUT; the tab is OUTPUT. The 8-pin WSON (DRJ) differs: pin 1 ADJ/GND, pins 2 to 4 VIN, pins 5 to 7 VOUT, pin 8 NC.
questions.notes: Figures tlv1117_c4_img0.jpg and img1.jpg plus the pin table.

questions.question: What capacitors and diode does the basic adjustable TLV1117 regulator circuit use?
questions.expected_answer: 10 uF on the input (Note C), 100 uF on the output (Note A), an optional CADJ on the ADJ pin (Note B), R1 and adjustable R2 as the divider, and a 1N4002 diode from output to input (Note D).
questions.notes: Figure 7-2 (tlv1117_c37_img0.jpg).

questions.question: What is the threshold voltage of the TLV1117's enable pin?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated: the TLV1117 has no enable pin. Its pins are ADJ/GND, INPUT, OUTPUT and, on WSON, NC.
questions.notes: Cross-document trap: the LM2596's ON/OFF pin has a 1.3 V threshold.

questions.question: How long is the TLV1117's soft-start time?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated. Page 1 says the fixed version (new chip) has an internal soft-start that reduces inrush current, but no time is given.
questions.notes: Fails if it invents a time.

questions.question: What switching frequency, load current and input voltage does the LM2596 support?
questions.expected_answer: 150 kHz fixed switching frequency, 3 A load current, and input up to 40 V (operating supply 4.5 V to 40 V; absolute maximum 45 V).

questions.question: How does the LM2596's ON/OFF pin work?
questions.expected_answer: Pulling it below about 1.3 V turns the regulator on; above 1.3 V (up to 25 V) shuts it down, dropping the input current to about 80 uA. Grounded or left open, the regulator stays on.

questions.question: How should the LM2596's catch diode be chosen?
questions.expected_answer: Current rating at least 1.3 times the maximum load current (or equal to the LM2596's current limit if it must survive a continuous short), reverse voltage at least 1.25 times the maximum input voltage, and fast: Schottky first, ultra-fast recovery acceptable, never 1N5400-series rectifiers. The example uses a 5 A, 20 V 1N5823.

questions.question: How does the LM2596 delayed start-up circuit work?
questions.expected_answer: As the input rises, capacitor C1 charges and pulls the ON/OFF pin high, keeping the regulator off. When the input settles and C1 stops charging, R2 pulls ON/OFF low and switching starts. R1 limits the ON/OFF pin voltage (25 V maximum) and C1's discharge current.

questions.question: What is the LM2596's oscillator frequency range?
questions.expected_answer: 127 kHz minimum, 150 kHz typical, 173 kHz maximum at TJ = 25 C; 110 kHz to 173 kHz from -40 C to 125 C.

questions.question: What is the LM2596's switch current limit?
questions.expected_answer: Peak current 3.6 A minimum, 4.5 A typical, 6.9 A maximum at TJ = 25 C; 3.4 A to 7.5 A from -40 C to 125 C.

questions.question: What efficiency does each LM2596 version reach at 3 A?
questions.expected_answer: 3.3 V version 73% (VIN = 12 V), 5 V version 80% (VIN = 12 V), 12 V version 90% (VIN = 25 V), adjustable version 73% (VIN = 12 V, VOUT = 3 V).
questions.notes: Ingestion trap: the efficiency rows are missing from the stored text of chunks 11 to 13; only some summaries keep them.

questions.question: What junction-to-ambient thermal resistance does the LM2596 have?
questions.expected_answer: TO-220: 50 C/W, mounted vertically with about 1 in2 of copper. TO-263: 50 C/W with 0.5 in2, 30 C/W with 2.5 in2 (single sided), and 20 C/W on a double-sided board with 3 in2 plus about 16 in2 on the other side (all 1 oz copper).
questions.notes: The conditions are footnotes; an answer without them is incomplete.

questions.question: What is the LM2596's pinout?
questions.expected_answer: Pin 1 VIN, pin 2 Output (switch), pin 3 Ground, pin 4 Feedback, pin 5 ON/OFF; the tab is ground.
questions.notes: Figure lm2596_c8_img0.jpg plus the pin table.

questions.question: In the fixed-output LM2596 application circuit, what optional output filter is shown and what layout advice does the figure give?
questions.expected_answer: An optional post ripple filter of 3 uH and a 180 uF low-ESR capacitor with short leads. The figure says to keep feedback wiring away from inductor flux, and to keep the heavy lines short with ground plane construction.
questions.notes: Only in the figure (lm2596_c38_img0.jpg).

questions.expected_answer: Not stated: the LM2596 has a fixed 150 kHz internal oscillator and no synchronisation pin; the datasheet does not describe synchronisation.

questions.question: What is the LM2596's soft-start time?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated. The absolute maximum table mentions an SD/SS pin and the electrical table has a SHUTDOWN/SOFT-START CONTROL heading, but the LM2596 has no soft-start pin and no soft-start time.
questions.notes: Trap: the table headings suggest a soft-start feature that this part does not document.

questions.question: How long does the LM555 LED-flasher example keep the LED on, and how were R and C chosen?
questions.expected_answer: The pulse width is t = 1.1 x R x C. For a 5 s delay RC = 4.545, so with R = 100 kohm, C = 45.4 uF; standard values R = 100 kohm and C = 47 uF were chosen. The measured delay was 5.17 s.
questions.notes: The schematic (Figure 17) shows 10 kohm and 470 uF instead; see lm555-09.

questions.question: What are the LM555's astable timing equations?
questions.expected_answer: Charge (output high) t1 = 0.693 (RA + RB) C; discharge (output low) t2 = 0.693 RB C; period T = 0.693 (RA + 2RB) C; frequency f = 1.44 / ((RA + 2RB) C).
questions.notes: Ingestion trap: the stored text of chunk 17 lost the t2 equation.

questions.question: What timing limits apply to the LM555's trigger and reset inputs?
questions.expected_answer: The minimum monostable pulse width is 10 us (comparator storage time when pin 2 is driven to ground). The reset-to-output delay is 0.47 us typical, and the minimum reset pulse width is 0.3 us. When reset is not used, connect it to VCC.

questions.question: What supply and bypassing does the LM555 need?
questions.expected_answer: A supply of 4.5 V to 16 V, bypassed with at least 0.1 uF in parallel with a 1 uF electrolytic capacitor, placed as close to the LM555 as possible.

questions.question: How much supply current does the LM555 draw?
questions.expected_answer: With the output low and no load: 3 mA typical, 6 mA maximum at VCC = 5 V; 10 mA typical, 15 mA maximum at VCC = 15 V. With the output high it is typically 1 mA less at 5 V.

questions.question: What are the LM555's trigger and threshold voltages?
questions.expected_answer: Trigger: 5 V at VCC = 15 V and 1.67 V at VCC = 5 V. Threshold: 0.667 x VCC. Trigger current 0.5 uA typical, 0.9 uA maximum.

questions.question: What is the LM555's junction-to-ambient thermal resistance for each package?
questions.expected_answer: PDIP 106 C/W, SOIC 170 C/W, VSSOP 204 C/W.
questions.notes: Cross-document trap: the NE555 gives different values for its packages.

questions.question: What is the largest total timing resistance (RA + RB) the LM555 allows?
questions.expected_answer: 20 Mohm for 15 V operation, set by the threshold current (footnote 5 of the electrical characteristics).
questions.notes: Cross-document trap: the NE555 says about 3.4 Mohm at 5 V and 10 Mohm at 15 V.

questions.question: What component values does the LM555 LED-flasher schematic (Figure 17) show?
questions.expected_answer: A 10 kohm timing resistor and a 470 uF timing capacitor (RC = 4.7 s), 0.01 uF on CONTROL VOLTAGE, a 470 ohm resistor in series with the LED, and a 10 kohm pull-up on TRIGGER with a pushbutton to ground; supply +5 V to +15 V. The text instead says R = 100 kohm and C = 47 uF (the same RC).
questions.notes: The figure (lm555_c19_img0.jpg) and the text disagree; a good answer reports what the figure shows and notes the difference.

questions.question: Using the LM555 free-running frequency graph, what frequency does RA + 2RB = 10 kohm with C = 0.01 uF give?
questions.expected_answer: About 14 kHz: f = 1.44 / ((RA + 2RB) C) = 1.44 / (10 kohm x 0.01 uF) = 14.4 kHz, consistent with the 10 kohm line in Figure 16.
questions.notes: Read from a log-log graph; accept about 10 kHz to 15 kHz.

questions.question: What is the LM555's maximum oscillation frequency?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated: the LM555 datasheet gives no maximum frequency.
questions.notes: Cross-document trap: the NE555 datasheet recommends 100 kHz or below.

questions.question: What is the LM555's charged-device-model (CDM) ESD rating?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated: only the human-body model rating is given, +/-500 V (SOIC package).
questions.notes: Cross-document trap: the NE555 gives CDM +/-1500 V.

questions.question: How do the NE555's trigger, threshold and reset inputs control the output?
questions.expected_answer: The trigger level is about one third of VCC and the threshold level about two thirds; both can be changed with the CONT pin. When TRIG falls below the trigger level, the flip-flop is set and the output goes high. When TRIG is above the trigger level and THRES above the threshold level, the flip-flop resets and the output goes low. RESET overrides all other inputs: when it is low, the output is low.

questions.question: What is the highest astable frequency recommended for the NE555?
questions.expected_answer: 100 kHz or below, to reduce distortion. For higher frequencies the datasheet suggests the TLC555 CMOS timer instead.

questions.question: How does the NE555 missing-pulse detector work, and what can it not detect?
questions.expected_answer: The input pulse train keeps retriggering the monostable timing interval. A missing pulse or a longer gap lets the interval complete, which produces an output pulse. An input stuck low cannot be detected, because the timing capacitor stays discharged. Choose RA x C greater than the maximum normal input high time.

questions.question: What sets the NE555's monostable pulse width, and what is its minimum?
questions.expected_answer: tw is about 1.1 x RA x C. TRIG must return high at least 10 us before the end of the timing interval, and the comparator storage time limits the minimum pulse width to 10 us.

questions.question: What operating temperature range does each 555 variant in the NE555 datasheet cover?
questions.expected_answer: NA555 -40 C to 105 C, NE555 0 C to 70 C, SA555 -40 C to 85 C, SE555 -55 C to 125 C.
questions.notes: Ingestion trap: chunk 5's stored text reads the NE555 row as 'NESS 0 C' and has lost the 70.

questions.question: How large can the NE555's timing resistors be?
questions.expected_answer: RA + RB is about 3.4 Mohm at VCC = 5 V and about 10 Mohm at VCC = 15 V, limited by the threshold current.
questions.notes: Cross-document trap: the LM555 says 20 Mohm.

questions.question: What ESD ratings does the NE555 have?
questions.expected_answer: +/-500 V human-body model and +/-1500 V charged-device model.

questions.question: What does the NE555 function table say the output and discharge switch do?
questions.expected_answer: RESET low: output low, discharge on. RESET high and TRIG below 1/3 VCC: output high, discharge off. TRIG above 1/3 VCC and THRES above 2/3 VCC: output low, discharge on. TRIG above 1/3 and THRES below 2/3 VCC: unchanged (as previously established).

questions.question: In the NE555 typical astable waveforms, what components are used, and what frequency and duty cycle result?
questions.expected_answer: RA = 5 kohm, RB = 3 kohm, C = 0.15 uF, RL = 1 kohm. That gives tH of about 0.83 ms, tL of about 0.31 ms, a frequency of about 870 Hz and an output-high duty cycle of about 73%.
questions.notes: The values are only legible in the figure (ne555_c14_img1.jpg); the frequency and duty cycle are computed with the datasheet's equations.

questions.question: From the NE555 output pulse duration graph, how long is the pulse with RA = 10 kohm and C = 1 uF?
questions.expected_answer: About 11 ms (about 10^-2 s on Figure 6-4), consistent with tw = 1.1 x RA x C.
questions.notes: Read from a log-log graph; accept 10 ms to 12 ms.

questions.question: What supply voltage range does the TLC555 support?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated: the NE555 datasheet only names the TLC555 CMOS timer as an alternative above 100 kHz and gives none of its specifications.

questions.question: What is the NE555's output short-circuit current limit?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated: there is no short-circuit current limit. The absolute maximum output current is +/-225 mA and the recommended output current is +/-200 mA; neither is a protection limit.
questions.notes: Fails if it presents +/-225 mA as a built-in current limit.

questions.question: When should an analog anti-aliasing filter be used instead of a digital filter, according to AN699?
questions.expected_answer: An analog filter acts before the A/D conversion. It removes out-of-band noise and interference, including noise peaks that could saturate the converter, and suits faster systems (above about 5 kHz). A digital filter acts after conversion: it uses oversampling and averaging, can remove noise injected during conversion, and is easy to make programmable, but it cannot remove noise peaks on the analog signal.

questions.question: In AN699's aliasing example with a 100 kHz sampling rate, where do 82 kHz, 219 kHz and 294 kHz inputs appear?
questions.expected_answer: Using fOUT = |fIN - N fS|: 82 kHz appears at 18 kHz, 219 kHz at 19 kHz and 294 kHz at 6 kHz.
questions.notes: The note's fifth example (347 kHz -> 53 kHz) is above fS/2 and is left out on purpose.

questions.question: What requirements does AN699's anti-aliasing design example set?
questions.expected_answer: Bandwidth DC to 1 kHz (cut-off 1 kHz or higher), at least 74 dB attenuation at 10 kHz, no gain or inversion, followed by a 12-bit SAR A/D converter sampling at 20 kHz (half of it is 10 kHz), whose ideal SNR is 74 dB.

questions.question: How do AN699's Bessel, Chebyshev and Butterworth implementations of the example compare?
questions.expected_answer: Bessel: 5th order, two Sallen-Key stages plus a passive pole, 79 dB attenuation at 10 kHz. Chebyshev: 3rd order, one Sallen-Key stage plus a passive pole, -70 dB at 10 kHz with 4 dB pass-band ripple. Butterworth: 4th order, two Sallen-Key stages, 80 dB at 10 kHz.
questions.notes: The three circuit figures (14, 15, 17) were not captured at ingestion.

questions.question: What errors does AN699's 3rd-order Chebyshev design introduce?
questions.expected_answer: It reaches -70 dB instead of the ideal -74 dB, which adds a little under 1/2 LSB of error from signals aliased between 10 kHz and 11.8 kHz, and its 4 dB ripple causes a 4 dB gain error in the pass band.

questions.question: Why are passive RC filters usually limited to a single pole in AN699?
questions.expected_answer: Their output impedance is high: a 1 kHz filter with a 0.1 uF capacitor needs a 1.59 kohm resistor, which can cause unwanted voltage drops or make impedance matching hard. An op amp stage isolates the filter's impedance from the next circuit.

questions.question: What are the Butterworth denominator coefficients for 2nd and 5th order filters in AN699?
What are the 4th-order Bessel denominator coefficients in AN699?

questions.question: At twice the cut-off frequency, roughly how much do AN699's 5th-order Butterworth, 0.5 dB Chebyshev and Bessel filters attenuate?
questions.expected_answer: About -30 dB for Butterworth, about -40 dB for the Chebyshev, and only about -12 dB for Bessel (Figure 4, normalised frequency 2).
questions.notes: Read from graphs (AN699_c8_img0.jpg); accept +/-5 dB.

questions.question: What is the DC gain of AN699's Sallen-Key filter, and which op amp does it use?
questions.expected_answer: K = 1 + R4 / R3, using an MCP601. With R3 open and R4 shorted the DC gain is 1 V/V.
questions.notes: Figure 10 (AN699_c13_img0.jpg) plus its caption.

questions.question: Which A/D converter part number does AN699's design example use?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated: it specifies only a 12-bit SAR A/D converter sampling at 20 kHz, with no part number.

questions.question: What is the group delay of AN699's 5th-order Bessel design?
questions.expected_answer: Not stated: AN699 says Bessel filters have a constant time delay over a wide frequency range but gives no group delay value for the design.
